system_prompt:
You are taking the TIMSS mathematics test for students in the eighth grade. Answer each question as well as you can.

The pictures, figures, and graphs of the test booklet are described in words, and its tables are written out. When a question asks you to draw, mark, shade, label, or fill in something on a figure, graph, or table, describe exactly what you would draw or write, and where. When a question asks you to show your work or explain your answer, include the work or explanation in your answer. For a multiple-choice question, choose one option.
user_prompt:
In this figure, triangles ABC and DEF are congruent with BC = EF .

[Image: Overlapping triangles ABC and DEF]

What is the measure of angle EGC ?

Figure, described in words:
Two overlapping triangles, ABC and DEF, resting on a shared horizontal baseline containing points B, E, C, and F in that order from left to right. Segment BC is the base of triangle ABC, and segment EF is the base of triangle DEF. Vertex A is above the baseline, and vertex D is to the right of A and also above the baseline. Side AC intersects side DE at point G. Angle B is labeled 40°, and angle F is labeled 60°.

A. 20°
B. 40°
C. 60°
D. 80°
E. 100°

answer.description: The letter of the option you choose for the question.
answer.title: Answer

llm_thinking:
Since BC corresponds to EF, the matching correspondence must be B↔E and C↔F, which means angle B equals angle E (40°) and angle C equals angle F (60°).

Now I'm working out angle EGC, the angle at intersection point G between lines AC and DE. Looking at triangle GEC, I trace angle GEC back to angle DEF, which corresponds to angle ABC under the mapping, giving 40°, and angle GCE back to angle ACB, corresponding to angle DFE, giving 60°.

Summing, 180 minus 40 minus 60 gives angle EGC as 80°, matching angle A — a consistent result confirming answer D.
